at øve.explanation: "At øve" means "to practice". Danish usually adds "mig" (myself): "Jeg øver mig i dansk" means "I am practicing Danish". The thing you practice comes after "i" (in).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **øve** mig i dansk hver dag.
sentence.en: I want to practice Danish every day.

en øl.explanation: "En øl" means "a beer". The plural is also "øl": "to øl" means "two beers". You can say "en stor øl" (a large beer) or "en lille øl" (a small beer).

sentence.da: Jeg er tørstig, så jeg drikker en kold **øl**.
sentence.en: I am thirsty, so I drink a cold beer.

et øje.explanation: "Et øje" means "an eye". "Hun har blå øjne" means "She has blue eyes" and "at lukke øjnene" means "to close your eyes".

sentence.da: Jeg har noget i mit **øje**, og det gør ondt.
sentence.en: I have something in my eye and it hurts.

et øjeblik.explanation: "Et øjeblik" means "a moment". "Et øjeblik, tak" means "One moment, please". The word is made of "øje" (eye) and "blik" (glance).

et øre.explanation: "Et øre" means "an ear". "Jeg har ondt i øret" means "My ear hurts", literally "I have pain in the ear".

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i mit **øre**, og jeg kan ikke høre godt.
sentence.en: My ear hurts and I cannot hear well.

øm.explanation: "Øm" means "sore" or "tender", when a part of the body hurts a little, especially when touched. It is milder than "ondt" (pain), as in "Jeg har ondt i armen" (My arm hurts).

sentence.en: My shoulder is sore after exercise.

øst.explanation: "Øst" means "east": "Vinden kommer fra øst" (The wind comes from the east).

sentence.en: The sun rises in the east.
